name: Congenital Pulmonary Airway Malformation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Radiologic and histopathologic diagnosis of CPAM

criteria.description: Presence of cystic or solid lung mass on prenatal or postnatal imaging
Histopathologic confirmation of abnormal airway tissue proliferation with cystic structures
Respiratory distress or recurrent pulmonary infections in neonate or infant

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic cystic or solid lung mass on imaging plus histopathologic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Prenatal ultrasound and CT imaging are critical for early diagnosis; histopathology is gold standard.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cystic lung mass detected on imaging
pathognomonic.notes: Typically identified prenatally or in early infancy
searchTerms: cystic mass in lung on imaging

pathognomonic.notes: Due to mass effect or lung hypoplasia

common.notes: Often due to cyst infection or impaired clearance
Increased respiratory rate secondary to compromised lung function
May occur in severe cases with hypoxia

common.symptomName: Decreased breath sounds over affected lung
searchTerms: reduced breath sounds over lung area

occasional.notes: Due to mass effect on thoracic cage

rare.notes: Secondary to chronic hypoxia or vascular compression
Severe mass effect causing displacement of mediastinal structures
Rare fetal complication due to large cystic lesions

laboratory: Generally nonspecific; may show leukocytosis if infected cysts present
imaging: Prenatal ultrasound showing cystic lung lesions
Chest X-ray revealing cystic or solid lung masses
CT scan demonstrating multicystic or solid lesions with air-fluid levels
genetic: No consistent genetic mutations identified; sporadic developmental anomaly
other: Histopathology showing cystic adenomatoid malformation of lung tissue

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of systemic arterial supply on imaging
Lack of communication with tracheobronchial tree
Overinflation of a pulmonary lobe without cystic lesions
Absence of discrete cystic masses on imaging
Located centrally near mediastinum rather than lung parenchyma

redFlags: Signs of infection or sepsis related to cystic lesions
references: Stocker JT. Congenital pulmonary airway malformation: a new name and expanded classification of congenital cystic adenomatoid malformation of the lung. Histopathology. 2002.
Laberge JM, Puligandla PS, Flageole H. Management of congenital cystic adenomatoid malformation of the lung. Paediatr Respir Rev. 2004.
Stocker JT. Pediatric lung tumors and cystic lung lesions. Mod Pathol. 2002.
